text:
maya: Heads-up — Acme onboarding: we're seeing a ~2.8x increase in 5xx and a bunch of timeouts over the last 24h. Can we get a quick endpoint breakdown? Key asks: top 3 failing URIs, error types (5xx/timeout/429), and any immediate mitigations. cc @aaron @jules
alerts-bot: incident-detection: anomaly detected for customer_id=acme, metric=5xx_rate, change=+180% over 3h — https://alerts.internal/acme/2068532100 :warning:
aaron: On it. initial look: spike started ~06:15 UTC. looks correlated with increased concurrent embeddings jobs from Acme. grabbing traces now.
jules: Pulled last 100 traces. Top failing endpoints (24h window): POST /v1/embeddings — mostly 503, count=238; POST /v1/chat/completions — 504s, count=89; POST /v1/generate — mixed 429/timeouts, count=42.
kevin: FYI Acme runs a scheduled nightly bulk job at ~06:00 UTC — could be saturating hosted pools. are they on Dedicated or Hosted?
maya: They're on Hosted (standard). explains the burst. Renewal risk: acct mgr mentioned latency hurts their UX; they flagged dedicated as a contingency during last call.
aaron: Short-term mitigations I recommend: 1) per-tenant rate limit for embeddings bursts (burst window), 2) route embeddings to quantized variant v-embed-q4 for lower mem/latency, 3) enable prefix KV cache for repeated requests. I can push a canary policy for Acme this morning.
jules: Logs snippet for the spike:
```
[06:17:02] 503 POST /v1/embeddings size=12 tokens=... conn=pool-full
[06:18:44] 504 POST /v1/chat/completions seq=... latency=45s
[06:19:10] 429 POST /v1/generate reason=timeout
```
maya: Can we run the canary now? I'll tell Acme the workaround + ETA. @aaron please include rollback plan.
aaron: Deploying canary routing for customer=acme -> v-embed-q4 and per-tenant limiter of 50 reqs/min. Monitoring: embedding success rate, queue length, tail latency. Will update in 10m :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: canary deploy started for customer=acme at 2068532150, routing policy v-embed-q4, limiter=50rpm — status=started
aaron: Quick follow-up: after 10m embeddings failures down from 238 -> 12 (5%), chat timeouts reduced ~60%. Keeping canary for 2h then evaluating.
maya: Great — for the weekly account health deck I'll capture: top failing endpoints, root cause = bursty onboarding bulk job on hosted pool, mitigation = canary routing + per-tenant limiter. Action items: (1) Offer Dedicated capacity + cost estimate, (2) add runbook detection for scheduled bursts, (3) follow up with Acme PM on optimizing their ingestion schedule. @kevin can you prep pricing?
kevin: On it — prepping dedicated pricing and a couple autoscale tweak suggestions for hosted pools to better absorb scheduled bursts.
maya: :white_check_mark: thanks everyone. I'll close this thread once stability is confirmed over the 2h window.
